submission.justification: S2 (gradient-boosted classifier, all variables including jet substructure) gives the highest expected significance in the statistical-only MC study: 4.14σ at 50% signal efficiency, versus 3.45σ for S1 and 2.61σ for S3 at the same working point. This matches the 2025 summary (4.1/3.4/2.6). A scan of S2 (30–70%) has a broad maximum at 50–60% (4.14σ at 50%, 4.12σ at 60%, 4.11σ at 55%). Differences that small are likely within MC noise, so I chose 50% as the centre of the plateau. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: The tool reports statistical uncertainty only, and no project document says anything about systematic uncertainties or how the background will be estimated. I therefore cannot show that the background estimate is robust. S2 relies on jet substructure variables, which are often poorly modelled in MC. Its systematic uncertainties could cut into its lead over S1 (a kinematics-only NN at about 3.4σ) or erase it. Before the selection freeze, the collaboration should check data/MC agreement for the input variables in control regions, define a data-driven background estimate, and redo the comparison with systematics included. If S2's background cannot be validated, S1 at about 50% efficiency is the next-best choice.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible expected signal significance
Selection must be one of the three strategies in candidate_specs.md

requirements.evidence: No document covers background systematics or control regions, and the simulation tool is statistical-only. S2 uses jet substructure, which may be poorly modelled. Needs validation before freeze.
Chosen working point is 50% signal efficiency.
